description: Padding share, TTFT and ITL under four prompt-length distributions at a common Poisson arrival rate. Tests whether 35.9% is a stack property or a workload property (review M5/Q5), and supplies the TTFT/ITL a serving paper is expected to report.
note_output_len: 64, not 1. Review M5(ii): output_len=1 leaves no decode steady state, so decode results were measured under a workload that barely decodes. 64 gives every request a decode phase long enough for an inter-token latency to mean something.
note_rate: 8 rps is below the saturation point measured in earlier sessions, so the arms compare packing rather than compare queueing collapse. Poisson, not closed-loop: a closed loop cannot produce the queueing that decides how steps pack.
note_lengths: Parametric families spanning the plausible range, NOT a production trace -- we have none and the paper says so. sigma=0.9 is the order of magnitude reported for chat prompt-length spread; the bimodal arm is the agentic shape (short turns plus long context). The result is a sensitivity range, not a corrected point estimate.
